newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea aims to hold CPI within 4.5 pct target.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea aims to hold CPI within 4.5 pct target.

text.p: South Korea's Finance Ministry said on Friday it would promote anti-inflation measures strongly to maintain the rise in the consumer price index (CPI) to within this year's target of 4.5 percent.

Private economists have said the CPI, South Koreas's leading inflation indicator, could rise more than five percent this year as depreciation of the won against the dollar pushes import prices higher.
The ministry said it would manage its monetary and foreign exchange policies flexibly to minimise inflationary pressure.
The ministry would enforce guidelines to keep wage increases in line with gains in productivity.
It will keep a close eye on prices for services, public utilities and industrial products.
Economic ministers will meet at 10.00 a.m. on Friday to work out details of the anti-inflation drive.
The CPI rose 4.7 percent in 1995. In the first eight months of this year it rose 4.4 percent, just slightly off the year's target.
